s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive back pain with systemic inflammation and neurological deficits
salient_findings: Neurological deficits including weakness, numbness, and difficulty with urination
key_facts: 1-month history of high fever, night sweats, and progressive back pain
Patient touched an unpasteurized sheep stomach with an injured hand about 1 month earlier
Initial outpatient therapy with oral cefprozil provided no lasting benefit
White-cell count of 7170/mm3 with 80% neutrophils
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 35 mm/hour
C-reactive protein level of 3.19 mg/dL
Procalcitonin level of 0.21 ng/mL
Serological test for tuberculosis was negative
Blood cultures grew a Gram-negative bacillus on hospital day 6
Developed weakness and numbness in both legs and difficulty with urination on hospital day 6
Neurologic examination revealed grade 3/5 strength in the right lower limb and grade 4/5 in the left
Hypertonia of both lower extremities and tenderness on percussion and palpation of the T9 and T10 spinous processes
Contrast-enhanced thoracic magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated an inflammatory lesion of the T9 lamina and a posterior epidural abscess compressing the spinal cord at T9–T10

shortlist.label: Spinal epidural abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has progressive back pain, systemic inflammation, and neurological deficits, with imaging showing an inflammatory lesion and a posterior epidural abscess compressing the spinal cord

shortlist.label: Vertebral osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has high fever, night sweats, and progressive back pain, with laboratory studies showing elevated inflammatory markers and imaging demonstrating osteolytic destruction of the neural arch

shortlist.label: Brucellosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient touched an unpasteurized sheep stomach with an injured hand, which is a risk factor for brucellosis, and has symptoms consistent with the disease

shortlist.label: Pott's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has progressive back pain, systemic inflammation, and neurological deficits, with imaging showing an inflammatory lesion, which could be consistent with spinal tuberculosis

shortlist.label: Pyogenic spondylitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has high fever, night sweats, and progressive back pain, with laboratory studies showing elevated inflammatory markers and imaging demonstrating an inflammatory lesion

raw.rationale: The patient developed weakness and numbness in both legs and difficulty with urination, and neurologic examination revealed grade 3/5 strength in the right lower limb and grade 4/5 in the left, with hypertonia of both lower extremities and tenderness on percussion and palpation of the T9 and T10 spinous processes. Contrast-enhanced thoracic magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated an inflammatory lesion of the T9 lamina and a posterior epidural abscess compressing the spinal cord at T9–T10, which is consistent with a spinal epidural abscess.

rejected.label: Vertebral osteomyelitis
rejected.why: While the patient has signs of vertebral infection, the presence of an epidural abscess and spinal cord compression is more specific for spinal epidural abscess.

rejected.label: Brucellosis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not specifically suggest brucellosis, and the presence of a Gram-negative bacillus in blood cultures and an epidural abscess is more consistent with a bacterial infection like spinal epidural abscess.

rejected.label: Pott's disease
rejected.why: The patient's serological test for tuberculosis was negative, making Pott's disease less likely.

rejected.label: Pyogenic spondylitis
rejected.why: While the patient has signs of vertebral infection, the presence of an epidural abscess and spinal cord compression is more specific for spinal epidural abscess.
